title: Stateless vs Stateful Application Failure Modes

nodes.label: Web Instance (Stateless)
nodes.detail: Stores no local sessions or uploads. Can be terminated at any second.

nodes.label: Replacement Instance
nodes.detail: Autohealed instantly; takes over traffic seamlessly.

nodes.label: Monolithic Local DB
nodes.detail: Stores database state on non-replicated local filesystem.

nodes.label: Cloud SQL HA Standby
nodes.detail: Synchronous regional replication with automated sub-minute failover.

steps.title: Steady-State Health Monitoring
steps.action: Health check probe sends heartbeat polling requests every 5 seconds to Web Instance (Stateless).
steps.why_traversal: Continuous active probing verifies that the instance is not merely powered on, but capable of processing application requests and database queries.
steps.narration: Hop 1: Health check probe continuously validates Web Instance (Stateless) response codes.

steps.title: Outage Trigger & Anomaly Detection
steps.action: Failure Trigger: Web Instance (Stateless) encounters threshold saturation or crash. Health check records 3 consecutive timeouts.
steps.why_traversal: Multi-probe threshold prevents transient network blips from triggering premature, expensive failovers.
steps.narration: Hop 2: Failure occurs on Web Instance (Stateless). Probe signals unhealthy threshold breach to Load Balancer.

steps.title: Automated Failover & Traffic Eviction
steps.action: Control plane withdraws Web Instance (Stateless) from forwarding table and redirects incoming traffic to standby unit Monolithic Local DB.
steps.why_traversal: Traffic reroutes in under 5 seconds across Google Andromeda SDN without DNS TTL delay or client reconfiguration.
steps.narration: Hop 3: Load balancer evicts Web Instance (Stateless) and reroutes active traffic to Monolithic Local DB.

steps.title: Capacity Recovery & Auto-Healing
steps.action: Auto-Healing: Managed Instance Group recreates failed instance and synchronizes state with Monolithic Local DB.
steps.why_traversal: MIG auto-healing restores full multi-zone redundancy, returning the cluster to balanced multi-active serving capacity.
steps.narration: Hop 4: Auto-healing restores capacity; Monolithic Local DB serves traffic while new unit initializes.

scenarios.label: Zone us-central1-a Complete Outage
scenarios.narration: Datacenter zone loses power. Stateless nodes seamlessly regenerate in Zone B; local database suffers total downtime until zone recovers.
scenarios.root_cause: Datacenter zone loses power. Stateless nodes seamlessly regenerate in Zone B; local database suffers total downtime until zone recovers.
scenarios.diverted_path: Normal request path is interrupted at Web Instance (Stateless), Monolithic Local DB. Downstream components receive timeout errors or drop packets without acknowledgment, forcing client retries or failover redirection.
scenarios.blast_radius: All user sessions dependent on Web Instance (Stateless), Monolithic Local DB experience elevated latency, HTTP 5xx errors, or severed connections.
scenarios.recovery: Deploy multi-region Anycast failover, cross-zone active-standby redundancy, automated health check eviction, and exponential backoff circuit breakers.

scenarios.label: Replacement Instance Network Degradation
scenarios.root_cause: Underlying Andromeda vSwitch queue saturation or hypervisor host maintenance causing 40% packet loss on Replacement Instance.
scenarios.diverted_path: Incoming TCP streams to Replacement Instance experience high retransmission rates and latency spikes up to 4500ms; gateway circuit breaker opens to shed load.
scenarios.blast_radius: Transactions processed by Replacement Instance slow down significantly; client applications encounter timeout errors.
scenarios.recovery: Configure client-side exponential backoff with full jitter; deploy Regional Managed Instance Groups with auto-healing and minimum 3-zone distribution.
scenarios.narration: Packet loss and connection timeouts detected on Replacement Instance. Circuit breaker trips to protect cluster.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.

purpose: Analyzes failure dynamics between stateless application tiers and stateful persistence systems, demonstrating graceful crash recovery versus split-brain data corruption risks.
routing_rationale: Stateless services can be evicted and recreated immediately across zones; stateful databases require quorum consensus (Paxos/Raft) and synchronous replication to survive node failures safely.
summary: Analyzes failure dynamics between stateless application tiers and stateful persistence systems, demonstrating graceful crash recovery versus split-brain data corruption risks.
